llm_top3.reasoning: MRK has by far the most material positive catalyst (successful Moderna/Merck cancer vaccine Phase 3 plus multiple upgrades and target hikes) despite a mid-tier quant rank. ADC pairs a top-2 quant rank with a clean fundamental beat, dividend hike and a $1M CEO buy. VTR offers a raised FY guidance and record senior housing NOI growth with strong secular demand. I skip top-ranked NTST because its equity offering dilution and WBS because its Santander deal price effectively caps upside.

NTST.reasoning: Q2 FFO/revenue beat, raised AFFO guidance, CEO insider buy and S&P SmallCap 600 inclusion outweigh dilution from the upsized equity offering.

ADC.reasoning: Agree Realty beat Q2 FFO, raised guidance, hiked dividend 4.3% and CEO bought $1M of stock; noise from unrelated ADC Therapeutics headlines is not applicable.

WBS.reasoning: Fed approved the Santander acquisition and shelf was terminated, so the outcome is largely fixed; remaining headlines are routine vesting filings.

EPRT.reasoning: Q2 FFO merely matched estimates with a revenue miss, insider COO selling 22,000 shares, and mixed valuation commentary.

CURB.reasoning: Q2 FFO/revenue beat with record acquisitions and updated guidance, but persistent heavy director (Otto) selling of millions in stock offsets.

MRK.reasoning: Merck/Moderna melanoma cancer vaccine Phase 3 success drove a 13% gain and multiple large price-target hikes and a Morgan Stanley upgrade, partly offset by an RBC downgrade.

AKR.reasoning: KeyBanc upgrade to Overweight, Truist target raise and raised FY26 FFO guidance, tempered by a 9M-share dilutive equity offering.

SBRA.reasoning: Q2 FFO/revenue beat and a Raymond James upgrade are offset by a GAAP loss from a loan write-off and a 15% seven-day slide.

CTRE.reasoning: Record $900M of investments at 8.9% yields and raised 2026 guidance, but the stock fell 5.9% and RBC downgraded to Hold.

CPB.reasoning: EPS beat and modest price-target raises to $22 with Hold/Neutral ratings, offset by GLP-1 demand destruction narrative and 31% short interest.

A.reasoning: Agilent won expanded EU and FDA approvals for PD-L1 companion diagnostics, a modest positive amid otherwise generic market noise.

VTR.reasoning: Ventas beat Q2 FFO, raised FY26 normalized FFO guidance and lifted investment volume expectations to $4.5B on strong senior housing demand.

TTEK.reasoning: Raised FY26 EPS guidance and record backlog plus a $49M NOAA contract, but revenue declined 4.5% YoY and shares slid on profit-quality doubts.

ABR.reasoning: Dividend cut 61% over two years, shares down ~52%, and continued credit/rate concerns despite a technically improving chart and Q2 beat chatter.

LEG.reasoning: Sales fell 6% with stock dropping post-earnings, but the pending Somnigroup merger caps downside with only a small remaining spread.

TMUS.reasoning: Downgrade citing new competitive pressures from satellite/Starlink and worst weekly performance in six years, only partly offset by Goldman's 35% upside call.

TAP.reasoning: Q2 EPS beat but GAAP pretax income fell 49% and guidance reaffirms an 11-15% underlying EPS decline amid category weakness.

DHR.reasoning: Potential bioprocessing tailwind from the Moderna/Merck cancer vaccine read-through and a large new Generation Investment position, but mostly routine 13F filings.

BF-B.reasoning: Board rejected Sazerac's $32/share takeover bid removing a near-term catalyst, and CEO retirement adds uncertainty amid soft spirits demand.

LEN.reasoning: Berkshire increased its Lennar stake meaningfully, but shares are down 28% with rising mortgage rates and weak order commentary weighing.
